newsitem.title: CHINA: China sees '97 spring tea output at 250,000 tonnes.
newsitem.headline: China sees '97 spring tea output at 250,000 tonnes.

text.p: China's output of spring season tea this year would reach 250,000 tonnes, up 4.6 percent from last year, the Farmers Daily said on Friday.
Total tea output value for the spring crop was expected to reach 4.4 billion yuan ($530.12 million), up 6.5 percent compared with the previous year, it said.

Customs statistics showed exports in the first five months reached 69,800 tonnes, up 34.2 percent against the same period last year, generating $116 million or an increase of 39.8 percent compared with 1996, it said.
However, the average price of well-known quality teas had fallen 10 percent to 33 yuan per kg and sales remained poor, it said.

The market price for well-known quality teas in eastern Fujian province had dropped 12.8 percent from last year's 30 yuan per kg while in neighbouring Zhejiang province it had fallen 200 yuan per kg from last year, it said.
Staple tea had performed better, with a large rise in export prices for black tea, it said.
The Ministry of Agriculture had forecast world tea output in 1997 would be lower than last year, it said.
The ministry expected the price of tea on the world market to drop due to increased supply and a slow rise in demand, it said.
As demand from major developing countries dropped, the price of tea from 1997 would move downwards, it said.
China's tea output in 1996 has been estimated at 510,000 tonnes.
